t: Section 2(a)(2)(J)(ii) of the John F. Kennedy Center Act (20 U.S.C. 76h(a)(2)(J)(ii)) is amended by striking “Public Works and Transportation” and inserting “Transportation and Infrastructure”.

fable.w: This is a technical conforming amendment that only updates the name of a congressional committee referenced in the John F. Kennedy Center Act. The tempting reading is that it touches the Kennedy Center's board membership, but the reference is to a House committee, which is inside the federal government. The amendment itself creates no consultation, hearing, comment process, or right to sue for any outside party.
fable.s: is amended by striking “Public Works and Transportation” and inserting “Transportation and Infrastructure”

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that only updates the name of a House committee in an existing statute. Congressional committees are inside the federal government, and the text brings in no outside party: no consultation, hearing, comment period, non-federal advisory body or right to sue. Being part of the Kennedy Center Act's governance provisions does not add outside participation to this section.
opus.s: is amended by striking “Public Works and Transportation” and inserting “Transportation and Infrastructure”.
opus.b:
**Step 1: Analysis.** The tempting reading is "Yes," because the amended provision belongs to the Kennedy Center's governance structure, which includes a Board of Trustees. But this section only renames a House committee, from "Public Works and Transportation" to "Transportation and Infrastructure." Congressional committees and their members are inside the federal government. No outside party is consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing or right to sue. So the answer is "No."

**Step 2: Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section is a clerical amendment that changes the name of a congressional committee referenced in another statute. It does not create any mechanism for outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) to consult with or participate in federal decision-making. Congress is inside the federal government, and renaming a committee does not constitute participation by outside entities.
qwen_chat.s: Section 2(a)(2)(J)(ii) of the John F. Kennedy Center Act (20 U.S.C. 76h(a)(2)(J)(ii)) is amended by striking “Public Works and Transportation” and inserting “Transportation and Infrastructure”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that amending the name of a congressional committee implies some form of consultation or participation with that committee. However, this is merely a clerical amendment to a statute's text regarding committee names. It does not establish a process for the public, states, or other outside entities to participate in a federal decision. The committee itself is part of the federal government (Congress), and renaming it does not involve outside parties.
